subject: pharmacology
title: Fluoroquinolones: Moxifloxacin, Ofloxacin, Targets, Tendon and QT, Nalidixic Acid and Nitrofurantoin

steps.tx: Fluoroquinolones trap bacterial **DNA gyrase** (topoisomerase II, primary in Gram negatives) and **topoisomerase IV** (primary in Gram positives) on DNA, converting them into double strand break machines that shred the chromosome, bactericidal and concentration dependent. Stepwise target mutations plus efflux and plasmid borne qnr protection genes erode the class; gatifloxacin's dysglycaemia exit and temafloxacin's haemolysis wrote early warnings that the class's convenience would always be audited by rare serious harms.
steps.say: Quinolones turn the bacterium's own enzymes into chromosome shredders; resistance edits the enzymes one step at a time.

nodes.label: Gyrase and topoisomerase IV trapped on DNA

steps.tx: Fluoroquinolones trap bacterial **DNA gyrase**, which is topoisomerase II and the main target in Gram negative organisms, and they also trap topoisomerase IV, the main target in Gram positive organisms. The frozen enzymes become machines for double strand breaks that shred the chromosome. Killing is bactericidal and concentration dependent. Resistance arrives by stepwise mutations in the targets, by efflux, and by plasmid borne qnr protection. Withdrawal of gatifloxacin for dysglycaemia and of temafloxacin for haemolysis showed early that convenience of the class is audited by rare serious harm.
steps.say: Fluoroquinolones lock DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV onto DNA so those enzymes break both strands and the chromosome fragments. The kill depends on concentration. Resistance edits the enzymes, pumps drug out, or arrives on plasmid qnr genes. Gatifloxacin and temafloxacin were withdrawn for serious metabolic and blood toxicity.

vis.alt: A fluoroquinolone is shown trapping DNA gyrase on bacterial DNA and producing double strand breaks.
vis.caption: The drug freezes DNA gyrase on the chromosome so the trapped enzyme cuts both DNA strands. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Moxifloxacin** extends the spectrum to anaerobes and tuberculosis (a second line and MDR regimen pillar) with once daily dosing, hepatic clearance and the class's strongest QT prolongation, while lacking urinary concentrations that forbid it in urinary infection, a formulary trap. **Ofloxacin**, levofloxacin's racemic parent, survives in second line tuberculosis history and topical eye and ear preparations where systemic warnings evaporate at microgram exposure.
steps.say: Moxifloxacin covers anaerobes and TB but never the urine; QT is its loudest warning.

left.title: Moxifloxacin
points: Once daily respiratory and intra abdominal roles

right.title: Ofloxacin
points: Racemate from which levofloxacin was refined
Topical ophthalmic and otic preparations common

steps.tx: **Tendon rupture** is the class's signature orthopaedic catastrophe: Achilles tendinitis progressing to rupture, risk multiplied by age over 60, steroids, renal failure, transplantation and sport, occurring during or months after therapy. Regulators boxed it alongside peripheral neuropathy (potentially irreversible), CNS effects and myasthenia exacerbation, reserving fluoroquinolones where alternatives exist for sinusitis, bronchitis and uncomplicated urinary infection. Any tendon pain on a quinolone stops the drug and the sport the same day.
steps.say: Tendon pain on a quinolone means stop today; the rupture does not send a second warning.

right.title: Risk multipliers
points: Age over 60 and corticosteroid co therapy
Previous quinolone tendon injury: never again

steps.tx: **QT prolongation** ranks within the class (moxifloxacin strongest, then levofloxacin, ciprofloxacin least) and stacks with hypokalaemia, bradycardia and the antiarrhythmic and antipsychotic QT shelves from earlier modules into torsades arithmetic. Dysglycaemia (both directions), photosensitivity, C difficile, aortic aneurysm and dissection signals in predisposed patients, and cartilage toxicity in juvenile animal studies fencing paediatric use to defined exceptions (anthrax, complicated urinary infection, cystic fibrosis) complete the audit list.
steps.say: QT, glucose, tendon, nerve, aorta: the quinolone audit is five systems long, so indications must be worth it.

nodes.label: Tendon, QT, glucose, nerve and aorta audit
Stop rules counselled: tendon pain, palpitations, paraesthesia

steps.tx: **Nalidixic acid**, the first generation quinolone without fluorination, survives as archaeology and a urine only agent whose rapid single step resistance retired it; its importance is genealogical (every fluoroquinolone descends from its naphthyridine scaffold) and mechanistic (proof that gyrase was druggable). Modern formularies that still stock it for urinary infection are practising history, and examinations ask it as the class's founding fossil.
steps.say: Nalidixic acid founded the family and retired on resistance; know it as the fossil, not the therapy.

left.title: Nalidixic acid
points: Urinary concentrations only, no systemic use
CNS effects and intracranial pressure in children historically

right.title: Fluorinated descendants
points: Fluorine and piperazine rings: potency and penetration
Generations widen Gram positive and anaerobic cover

steps.tx: **Nitrofurantoin** is reduced by bacterial flavoproteins into reactive intermediates that shatter multiple bacterial targets at once, which is why resistance stays rare after seventy years, and why its therapeutic universe is the bladder: serum and tissue levels are subtherapeutic, forbidding pyelonephritis and bacteraemia use absolutely. It owns uncomplicated cystitis and long term prophylaxis in pregnancy compatible windows (avoided at term for neonatal haemolysis), with eGFR floors debated between 30 and 45.
steps.say: Nitrofurantoin is a bladder only drug of rare resistance; pyelonephritis on it is a prescribing error.

left.title: Nitrofurantoin strengths
points: Multi target bacterial damage, resistance rare
Preserves gut flora relatively, low C difficile

right.title: Nitrofurantoin fences
points: No tissue levels: never pyelonephritis or sepsis
eGFR below 30 to 45: ineffective and toxic
Avoid at term and in G6PD neonates

steps.tx: **Chronic nitrofurantoin writes** its own toxicology chapter: acute eosinophilic pneumonitis weeks in, chronic fibrotic lung injury and hepatitis months to years into prophylaxis, and peripheral neuropathy where renal impairment accumulates it. Long term users earn periodic liver, lung and symptom review, and any new cough, breathlessness or jaundice on prophylaxis stops the drug pending workup, because fibrosis caught late does not forgive.
steps.say: Years of prophylaxis can scar lungs and liver; new breathlessness on nitrofurantoin stops it first and investigates second.

nodes.label: Months to years of nitrofurantoin prophylaxis
New cough, breathlessness, jaundice or paraesthesia
Stop drug, image and test liver and lungs
Prophylaxis indication re justified or retired

steps.tx: **Chelation governs quinolone** absorption absolutely: aluminium and magnesium antacids, iron, calcium, zinc and sucralfate bind the drug in the gut into uselessness, spacing by two hours before or four to six after is prescription information as important as dose, and enteral feeds do the same silently in tube fed patients. Cystic fibrosis, anthrax and febrile neutropenia protocols keep paediatric and specialist doors open where the class warnings bend to indications that outweigh them.
steps.say: Cations cage quinolones in the gut; spacing rules are dosing rules, not dietary advice.

left.title: Chelation culprits
points: Antacids, iron, calcium and zinc supplements
Enteral feeds in tube fed patients

right.title: Where warnings bend
points: Complicated urinary infection in children by specialists
